papers.title: The pharmacological potential and metabolic risks of Xiaojin Pill in sorafenib-resistant papillary thyroid carcinoma: an integrated network analysis.
papers.abstract: Sorafenib resistance limits the efficacy of treatments for advanced papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The antitumor potential of Xiaojin Pill (XJP) has been demonstrated, yet its mechanisms potentially implicated in sorafenib resistance and combinational toxicological risks remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the molecular mechanisms through which XJP may act on signaling pathways implicated in sorafenib resistance, and to assess its combinational toxicological risks during co-administration with sorafenib.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated network analysis to predict how Xiaojin Pill (XJP), a traditional Chinese medicine, might act on signaling pathways involved in sorafenib resistance in papillary thyroid carcinoma, and to assess toxicological risks when combined with sorafenib. The work is largely computational and hypothesis-generating, identifying candidate mechanisms and potential combination safety concerns without experimental validation.

papers.title: A broadly active flavivirus NS4B targeting compound that blocks NS4B-NS3 binding and replication organelle formation.
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses, including West Nile virus (WNV), dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), cause substantial global morbidity and mortality, yet no broadly effective direct-acting antivirals are available. The viral nonstructural protein NS4B has emerged as a promising antiviral target, although the compounds described to date are largely DENV-specific. Here we characterize SRI-38841, a xanthine analog derived from hit-to-lead optimization of a previously described WNV inhibitor, which inhibits WNV replication with an IC₉₀ of 0.87 µM and l
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors characterize SRI-38841, a xanthine analog optimized from a prior West Nile virus inhibitor, that blocks replication of multiple mosquito-borne flaviviruses (WNV, DENV, ZIKV, JEV) with sub-micromolar potency. The compound works by disrupting the interaction between viral NS4B and NS3 proteins, thereby preventing formation of the replication organelles the virus needs to replicate. This represents a promising broadly active direct-acting antiviral scaffold against a family of pathogens with no approved therapeutics.

papers.title: PHENOMS: Open-Source Software for Rust-Accelerated Hydrogen-Bond Analysis in Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) provides powerful insight into protein structure and dynamics, but interpretation of protection patterns at atomic resolution often requires complementary computational modeling. We present PHENOMS, an open-source Python package that integrates molecular dynamics trajectories with HDX-MS data to analyze backbone hydrogen-bond networks by tracking how individual hydrogen bonds and residue-residue contacts form, break, and reorganize throughout the simulations. This residue-level analysis can reveal local structural changes that may be misse
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: PHENOMS is an open-source Python package that combines molecular dynamics trajectories with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) data to analyze backbone hydrogen-bond networks at residue-level resolution. It tracks how individual hydrogen bonds and residue contacts form, break, and reorganize over simulation time, revealing local structural changes that may be missed by other methods. The tool uses Rust-accelerated computation for efficiency.

papers.title: Forecasting and Dynamics of Huntington's disease: A Machine Learning approach for Fractional-Order Mathematical Model.
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by expansion of CAG repeats in the HTT gene, leading to accumulation of mutant huntingtin and progressive neuronal dysfunction, particularly in vulnerable brain regions such as the striatum. Although length of CAG repeats is a major determinant of the risk of disease, it does not account for all the variance in age of onset, rate of progression or region of neurodegeneration. The aim of this work was to construct a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the potential role of pure, interrupted and m
papers.summary: This paper builds a fractional-order mathematical model of Huntington's disease progression and couples it with machine learning to forecast disease dynamics. The model incorporates the effects of pure, interrupted, and mosaic CAG repeat patterns, aiming to explain variability in age of onset and progression beyond repeat length alone. It represents a modeling and forecasting contribution rather than an experimental or clinical study.

papers.title: Electrochemical Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Free Energy Surfaces from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) is an elementary step in many electrocatalytic reactions, yet molecular-level descriptions of solvent reorganization energetics in these reactions remain limited. Herein, we describe a first-principles computational platform to calculate free energy surfaces and quantify reorganization energies for interfacial electrochemical PCET. Hydrogen electrosorption at Pt(111)/water interfaces is used as a model reaction to derive PCET free energy surfaces using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations in an explicit solvent. The reaction is described as a non-adi
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.summary: The authors present a first-principles computational platform that uses ab initio molecular dynamics with explicit solvent to compute free energy surfaces and reorganization energies for electrochemical proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) at electrode-water interfaces. They demonstrate the approach on hydrogen electrosorption at a Pt(111)/water interface, treating the reaction as a non-adiabatic process. This provides a molecular-level route to quantify solvent reorganization energetics that were previously difficult to access for interfacial electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Structural and Energetic Determinants of Monobody Recognition of Oncogenic KRAS Variants.
papers.abstract: Monobodies are engineered binding proteins that recognize extended protein surfaces and offer advantages over small-molecule inhibitors for targeting challenging KRAS oncoproteins. Monobody 12D4 exhibits high affinity and selectivity for the oncogenic KRAS(G12D) mutant, but the molecular determinants governing its recognition and the basis for its mutant selectivity remain poorly understood. Here, we combined molecular dynamics simulations and energy calculations to characterize the interactions between monobody 12D4 and WT KRAS as well as four clinically relevant oncogenic variants (G12C, G12
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations and energy calculations to dissect how the engineered monobody 12D4 binds oncogenic KRAS variants, focusing on its high affinity and selectivity for KRAS(G12D). The work identifies structural and energetic features that distinguish mutant recognition from wild-type KRAS, offering a mechanistic basis for designing variant-selective binders against challenging KRAS oncoproteins.

papers.title: Unraveling Hierarchical Structure in Ionic Liquid-Extractant Mixtures with X-ray Scattering.
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid extraction (LLE) is the predominant method for the selective recovery and separation of many critical materials, including rare earth elements and platinum group metals. Ionic liquids (ILs) have been proposed to replace traditional solvents in LLE to enhance or manipulate separation performance. The tunable nanostructure of ILs is a unique and defining characteristic that impacts their function, but how that structure is affected by mixing with the LLE extractant is not understood. To investigate this, we combine small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and molecular dynamics (MD) sim
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses small-angle X-ray scattering combined with molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how the nanoscale structure of ionic liquids changes when mixed with liquid-liquid extraction extractants. The work reveals hierarchical structural organization in these mixtures, which is important for understanding and optimizing ionic liquids as replacements for traditional solvents in critical material separations such as rare earth and platinum group metal recovery.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics and preliminary experimental validation suggest the therapeutic potential of lycorine in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) is one of the most prevalent gynecological malignancies worldwide and remains a significant threat to women's health. Lycorine, a natural alkaloid isolated from plants of the Amaryllidaceae family, has attracted considerable attention owing to its diverse pharmacological activities, particularly its anti-tumor properties. However, the potential therapeutic targets and action mechanism of lycorine in UCEC remain unclear.In this study, an integrated strategy combining bioinformatic analysis and preliminary experimental validation was used to elucidate
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatic analysis with preliminary experimental validation to explore how lycorine, a natural plant alkaloid, might act against uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC). The authors identify potential therapeutic targets and propose mechanisms of action, suggesting lycorine has anti-tumor potential in this gynecological cancer. The work is exploratory and relies on computational prediction plus limited wet-lab confirmation.

papers.title: Cross-Linking Simulation at Metal Oxide-Thermoset Interfaces Using Quantum Chemical and Molecular Dynamics Methods.
papers.abstract: Understanding how oxidized metal surfaces catalyze the curing of epoxy resins is essential in improving the reliabilities of epoxy-metal oxide interfaces in multimaterial systems. The catalytic effects of hydroxylated oxidized tin metal (SnO2) surfaces on the cross-linking of epoxy resins were investigated using a hybrid approach that combined quantum chemical calculations with molecular dynamics simulations, wherein the reaction kinetics were modeled using Monte Carlo techniques. Analyzing the reaction pathways and spatial distributions at different hydroxylation levels revealed that fully hy
papers.summary: This study uses quantum chemical calculations combined with molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo reaction modeling to investigate how hydroxylated tin oxide (SnO2) surfaces catalyze epoxy resin curing. The authors show that the degree of surface hydroxylation strongly influences reaction pathways and the spatial distribution of cross-linking at the epoxy–metal oxide interface. The work provides a multiscale simulation framework for understanding and potentially tuning adhesion in multimaterial epoxy–metal systems.

papers.title: Cytoplasmic Expression of Papain Isozymes in Engineered Escherichia coli for Substrate Selectivity and Computational Insights.
papers.abstract: Challenges in isolating individual papain isozymes from papaya latex and in producing full-length, correctly folded, and soluble recombinant papain isozymes in Escherichia coli have limited detailed investigations into their distinct enzymatic properties and substrate specificities. In this study, we report the successful high-yield cytoplasmic expression of papain, protease omega, proteinase IV (pro-IV), and chymopapains I, II, and III in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains and a comprehensive investigation of their distinct biochemical and computational mechanistic insights. Building upon our
papers.summary: The authors achieved high-yield cytoplasmic expression of six papain-family isozymes (papain, protease omega, proteinase IV, and chymopapains I–III) in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains, overcoming prior difficulties in producing soluble, correctly folded recombinant papain isozymes. They then characterized the distinct biochemical properties and substrate selectivities of each isozyme and complemented the experimental work with computational mechanistic analyses. This provides a platform for studying individual papain isozymes that are hard to isolate from papaya latex.

papers.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid en
papers.summary: Poké is a new computational tool that identifies ligandable pockets on protein surfaces by combining energetic mapping with a neural-network-based scoring system. It can rapidly detect binding sites in both static protein structures and long molecular dynamics trajectories, including cryptic sites that only appear after conformational changes. This makes it useful for structure-based drug design where finding druggable pockets is a key first step.

papers.title: Weighted Views Representation with Multi-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction.
papers.abstract: We extend the weighted-views molecular featurization framework (d'Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp, and Zunger, 2011) by enriching it with single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information. We use these enriched views within a machine-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network. We demonstrate performance competitive with the state-of-the-art on the QM7 atomization energy benchmark (regression), ranking enantiomers by their docking scores (trained
papers.summary: This paper extends a weighted-views molecular featurization framework by adding single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information, then feeds these enriched views into a Transformer architecture whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions. The method achieves competitive performance on the QM7 atomization energy regression benchmark and on ranking enantiomers by docking scores. It is a methodological contribution to molecular property prediction using physics-informed attention.

papers.title: OPC3/LEW: A New Flexible Three-Site Water Model to Simulate Low-Electrostatic Environments.
papers.abstract: One of the main goals of computational simulations is to closely reproduce the environmental conditions in which biomolecules perform their physiological functions. However, the choice of water model is often based more on computational cost than on its effect on the molecular environment, as is the case with membrane proteins. These systems fulfill their biological function in low-polarity molecular environments that the most common or currently available water models do not reproduce accurately. In this work, we present a new flexible water model with three interaction sites that accurately
papers.summary: The authors introduce OPC3/LEW, a new flexible three-site water model designed to better reproduce low-electrostatic (low-polarity) environments such as those found around membrane proteins. The model aims to address the tendency of standard water models to misrepresent these environments, which is often overlooked in favor of computational cost. This provides a tool for more physiologically realistic simulations of membrane protein systems.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors.
papers.abstract: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are i
papers.summary: This study trains machine learning models on molecular dynamics data from over 6,000 amorphous polymer electrolyte systems to predict four key transport properties, including ionic conductivity and diffusivity. By using chemically informed structural descriptors, the approach aims to capture the complex coupling between polymer chemistry, structure, and ion dynamics. The work offers a data-driven route to screening polymer electrolytes for next-generation lithium batteries without exhaustive simulation.

papers.title: AOXP: An Integrated Framework for Antioxidant Peptide Prediction Leveraging LLM-Based Semantic Features and Optimized Physicochemical Ensembles.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress is a critical driver of various severe diseases, positioning antioxidant peptides (APs) as promising therapeutic agents. However, their discovery is constrained by the limitations of low-throughput wet-lab assays and insufficient computational prediction tools. To address this, we developed Antioxidant Peptides eXplorer (AOXP), a deep learning framework that leverages multiscale feature integration for high-precision AP prediction. Unlike existing models that often rely on isolated sequence patterns or manual feature descriptors, AOXP employs a hybrid encoding strategy that sy
papers.summary: AOXP is a deep learning framework for predicting antioxidant peptides that combines LLM-derived semantic features with optimized physicochemical descriptors in a hybrid encoding strategy. It aims to overcome the low throughput of wet-lab assays and the limitations of existing computational tools that rely on isolated sequence patterns or manual features. The work presents an integrated multiscale feature approach for high-precision peptide prediction.

papers.title: Cytotoxic Activity and Molecular Docking Studies of ONNO Type Salophen Schiff Base Metal Complexes.
papers.abstract: A Schiff base ligand (H2L) was synthesized through the condensation of 3,5-dibromo-2-hydroxybenzaldehyde with 1,2-phenylenediamine and subsequently complexed with Cu(II), Ni(II), Pt(II), Fe(II), and Pd(II) ions. Synthesized compounds were examined using FT-IR, UV-Vis, NMR, mass, elemental analysis, molar conductivity, and magnetic susceptibility. The H2L and transition metal complexes were tested for their cytotoxic activity potential against human liver carcinoma (HepG2) and lung adenocarcinoma (A549) cell lines. The cytotoxic activities of compounds were determined based on their IC50 values
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of a salophen-type Schiff base ligand and its Cu(II), Ni(II), Pt(II), Fe(II), and Pd(II) complexes, evaluated for cytotoxicity against HepG2 liver and A549 lung cancer cell lines. Molecular docking studies were used to rationalize the observed cytotoxic activity. The work is a standard coordination chemistry and preliminary anticancer screening study.

papers.title: Integrated Computational Pipeline Combining Metabolomics and Network Pharmacology for Bioactive Scaffold Discovery: Application to Antarctic Moss Chorisodontium aciphyllum.
papers.abstract: Discovering lead compounds from complex natural matrices traditionally requires resource-intensive isolation steps. Integrating computational biology with untargeted metabolomics offers a more efficient alternative for rapid target prediction and screening. Here, we present a computational pipeline combining LC-MS/MS metabolomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking to identify bioactive scaffolds. We applied this approach to the methanolic extract of the Antarctic moss Chorisodontium aciphyllum as a model matrix. Profiling the bioactive fraction (Fr.3) identified 17 secondary metaboli
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational pipeline that combines LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking to identify bioactive compounds from complex natural product mixtures without extensive isolation. Applied to the Antarctic moss Chorisodontium aciphyllum, the workflow profiled 17 secondary metabolites in a bioactive fraction and predicted their likely protein targets and binding interactions. The approach offers a faster, resource-efficient alternative to traditional bioassay-guided isolation for natural product lead discovery.

papers.title: PEG10/TRIB3 axis is associated with malignant behavior and Notch-related signaling in oral squamous cell carcinoma cells.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is an aggressive oral epithelial neoplasm for which the expression of paternally expressed gene 10 (PEG10) has notable prognostic implications. However, the functional role of this protein in OSCC remains to be fully elucidated. The present study aimed to explore the function of PEG10 in regulating OSCC cell behavior and the potential mechanisms of this regulation. Cell Counting Kit-8, 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine, wound healing and Transwell assays were employed to estimate cell proliferation, migration and invasion, respectively. Furthermore, flow cytometry a
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of PEG10 in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, using proliferation, migration, and invasion assays to show that PEG10 promotes malignant behavior. The authors identify a PEG10/TRIB3 axis linked to Notch-related signaling, suggesting a mechanistic pathway underlying OSCC aggressiveness. The work extends prior prognostic observations of PEG10 to a functional role in OSCC cell biology.

papers.title: From agricultural waste to functional gels: Mulberry pomace-derived carboxymethyl cellulose synergistically enhances calcium-mediated peanut protein isolate gelation.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop a sustainable functional ingredient from mulberry pomace-derived carboxymethyl cellulose (MPCMC) and elucidate its synergistic role with Ca2+ in regulating peanut protein isolate (PPI) gelation. MPCMC was prepared and its effects on PPI gel properties and underlying mechanisms were systematically investigated through multiscale characterization, intermolecular force analysis, correlation analysis, and molecular docking simulation. Results showed that 1.5% MPCMC plus 12 mM Ca2+ increased PPI gel strength from 52.47 g to 142.89 g and water holding capacity from 72.21%
papers.summary: This study extracts carboxymethyl cellulose from mulberry pomace (an agricultural waste) and shows that adding it together with calcium ions substantially improves the strength and water-holding capacity of peanut protein isolate gels. Multiscale characterization and molecular docking suggest the polysaccharide and Ca2+ act synergistically to reinforce the protein gel network, offering a sustainable route to functional food ingredients.

papers.title: Identification of Neuroinflammation-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: An Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approach.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a liver disease that progresses and may be connected to neuroinflammation, though the specific molecular mechanisms are not yet understood. The objective of this research was to explore candidate diagnostic biomarkers related to neuroinflammation-associated gene programs for MASH through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, as a hypothesis-generating study.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated bioinformatics and machine learning to identify candidate diagnostic biomarkers for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) that are linked to neuroinflammation-related gene programs. The authors frame the work as hypothesis-generating, aiming to uncover molecular connections between liver disease progression and neuroinflammation. Specific biomarkers and validation results are not detailed in the abstract.

papers.title: Carbonic anhydrase 4 restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention.
papers.summary: This study identifies carbonic anhydrase 4 (CA4) as a key regulator that restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis. The findings suggest CA4 loss promotes fibrotic progression through dysregulated innate immune activation, highlighting a potential molecular target for diagnosis and intervention.

papers.title: Comparative multi-target computational profiling of ebelin lactone across cognition-associated proteins.
papers.abstract: Ebelin lactone (EL) is a bacoside-related triterpenoid derivative produced through acid hydrolysis and has previously shown binding affinity toward the M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors. However, its structural compatibility with proteins involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress responses, and neurite remodeling has not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens ebelin lactone, a triterpenoid derived from bacosides, against multiple proteins linked to cognition, including targets involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress, and neurite remodeling. It extends prior findings of binding to M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors by profiling structural compatibility across a broader set of cognition-associated proteins. The work is purely computational docking/profiling and does not include experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated pharmacology and validation reveal Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 to modulate prostate cancer immune microenvironment via ROS/STAT3-driven chemokine reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is responsible for a substantial proportion of male cancer cases worldwide. Biochemical recurrence (BCR) representing a critical challenge in its disease management. Formononetin, a natural isoflavone derived from traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential anticancer properties. We sought to determine the translational potential of Formononetin-targeted molecules in PCa.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated pharmacology and experimental validation to show that the natural isoflavone Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 in prostate cancer cells, which alters ROS/STAT3 signaling and reprograms chemokine expression to modulate the tumor immune microenvironment. The authors propose this pathway as a potential avenue for addressing biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. Predicting the consequences of mutations on structure and function in proteins can be accomplished by using computational methods, which are relatively inexpensive and rapid compared with experimental methods. Here, we used a multidimensional in silico approach
papers.summary: This study uses multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations to examine how mutations at the IL-17A–IL-17RA protein interface perturb the structure and dynamics of the complex. The authors aim to predict which mutations disrupt the interaction, with the goal of informing therapeutic strategies that block IL-17A signaling in inflammatory autoimmune diseases. The work is a computational, simulation-based analysis rather than an experimental validation study.

papers.title: Quercetin ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced placental dysfunction by modulating the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network.
papers.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) induces placental structural and functional disturbances associated with dysregulated AGE-RAGE/ROS signaling and inflammatory responses. Existing flavonoid-related studies merely observed changes in pathway protein levels, lacking direct experimental proof of molecular binding between candidate compounds and core receptors. This study aimed to investigate the potential involvement of RAGE in the protective effects of quercetin and to characterize the associated AGE-RAGE/ROS/NF-κB-related signaling changes in GDM placental injury.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether quercetin protects against placental dysfunction caused by gestational diabetes mellitus by targeting the AGE-RAGE signaling pathway. The authors provide experimental evidence of molecular binding between quercetin and RAGE, and characterize downstream changes in ROS and NF-κB inflammatory signaling in GDM placental injury models. The work moves beyond prior flavonoid studies that only observed pathway protein changes by directly demonstrating compound-receptor binding.

papers.title: Kurarinol A from Sophora flavescens suppresses hepatic stellate cell activation via the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB pathway.
papers.abstract: Sophora flavescens is traditionally used in TCM and Miao/Mongolian/Yi ethnomedicines for hepatobiliary disorders, yet its bioactive flavonoid constituents and mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the anti-hepatic fibrosis efficacy, mechanism, and target of the ethyl acetate fraction (EAF) from S. flavescens and its key lavandulyl flavonoid kurarinol A (KA).
papers.summary: This study identifies kurarinol A, a flavonoid from the traditional medicinal plant Sophora flavescens, as a suppressor of hepatic stellate cell activation—the key cellular event in liver fibrosis. The authors show the compound acts through the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway, providing a mechanistic rationale for the plant's traditional use in liver disorders.

papers.title: SLC5A12 defines an invasive epithelial state associated with immune remodeling and therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by marked epithelial and immune heterogeneity. The malignant epithelial states associated with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and potential therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study identifies SLC5A12 as a marker of an invasive epithelial state in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), linking this state to immune remodeling within the tumor microenvironment. The authors propose that this epithelial state represents a potential therapeutic vulnerability, though the abstract does not detail the specific experimental or computational evidence supporting these claims.

papers.title: Integrated machine learning and in vitro pipeline for TRPA1-active chemesthetic flavor compounds: From predictive screening to molecular mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Chemesthesis constitutes a fundamental dimension of food sensory perception, triggered by transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) ion channels that mediate responses to pungent and irritating flavor compounds. However, efficient prediction of TRPA1 activation by flavor compounds remains limited by the low throughput of traditional experimental screening. Here, we developed an integrated computational and in vitro pipeline to overcome this limitation. Using an optimized Random Forest (RF) machine learning model, we successfully predicted and screened representative flavor compounds. We e
papers.summary: The authors built a Random Forest machine-learning model to predict which flavor compounds activate the TRPA1 ion channel, the receptor behind pungent and tingling sensations in food. They then validated top predictions with in vitro assays and explored the molecular mechanisms of activation. This integrated screening pipeline aims to replace slow, low-throughput experimental testing with faster computational triage.

papers.title: Unveiling Molecular Basis of Terminalia chebula in Modulating the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB Axis in Diabetic Nephropathy: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Computational Study.
papers.abstract: AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. A total of 357 phytoconstituents were retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 and PubChem databases and screened through SwissADME and pkCSM, yielding 14 bioactive, drug-like, and no
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and computational modeling to predict how compounds from the medicinal plant Terminalia chebula might act against diabetic nephropathy. Starting from 357 phytochemicals, the authors filtered to 14 drug-like compounds and mapped them onto the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB signaling axis, suggesting a multi-target mechanism. The work is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: Expression of Concern: Discovery of ROCK2 inhibitors through computational screening of ZINC database: Integrating pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and MD simulations.
papers.summary: This is an Expression of Concern notice from PLOS ONE regarding a previously published study that used computational screening of the ZINC database, pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and MD simulations to identify ROCK2 inhibitors. The notice does not report new scientific findings; it flags concerns about the integrity or reliability of the published work. Readers should consult the notice for the specific issues raised and any subsequent editorial action.
